source.title: Hands-On IAM Labs - Lab 2: Setting Up Multi-Factor Authentication
source.author: Andrew

evidence_scope: The package documents the supplied training guide. All screenshots are the guide author's example screenshots. Configuration and results are source-described, source-illustrated or expected; personal execution and successful outcomes have not been verified.
not_included: Passwords, enrollment QR codes, TOTP secrets, one-time codes or backup codes
Test results, recovery outcomes or security metrics from the portfolio owner's environment
An emergency bypass, command-line recovery or break-glass procedure (not described by the guide)
redaction_summary: Every one of the 52 figures was inspected individually for passwords, QR codes, TOTP secrets, one-time codes, backup codes, tokens, session identifiers and personal information. Screens that carry or could carry enrollment material (2.20, 2.21, 2.22, 2.26), backup codes (2.44), populated codes (2.29) or password entry (2.2, 2.17, 2.19) were excluded rather than redacted, so no redaction was needed. In the source, QR codes, codes, backup codes and IPs had already been replaced with placeholders by the author. Selected screenshots were re-encoded with Pillow, which drops PNG metadata chunks.

limitations: Personal completion of the lab and of any optional scenario is not verified.
WebAuthn cannot be completed on the guide's plain HTTP lab; no WebAuthn result exists.
The NIST SP 800-63B-4 statements (SMS restricted, email not for out-of-band, OTP not phishing-resistant) are attributed to the guide and were not independently verified against the standard.
Lost-device re-enrollment depends on the user remaining in scope of the force-configure validation stage.
Admin self-recovery after losing the only factor is not possible from the browser; the guide offers backup codes as a mitigation and describes no break-glass procedure.
Prerequisites from Lab 0 and Lab 1 (instance setup, synced accounts) are assumed, not verified.
Figure 2.42 does not visually distinguish member and non-member results; conditional-MFA behavior is source-described.
